sources.title: 了解 Gemini Notebook (Learn about Gemini Notebook)
directly_supported_observations: System provides inline citations from uploaded sources (PDF, websites, YouTube videos, audio files, Google Docs, Google Slides)
Gemini Notebook designed to answer questions based on information provided in uploaded sources
System distinguishes three failure modes: safety flagging, unclear phrasing, no relevant information in sources
For Workspace/Education users: uploaded content NOT used for AI training; NOT subject to human review
Chinese official page accessed; product may be called Gemini Notebook or NotebookLM
design_implications: Source-bound AI architecture demonstrated as product feature
Material scope enforcement requires explicit failure mode messages
Citation mechanism presented as accuracy/transparency/trust feature
File upload pattern establishes basic course boundary
limitations_and_non_inferences: No learning effectiveness evidence provided
No pedagogical action specification
No learner modeling capability described
Product status uncertain (naming: Gemini Notebook vs. NotebookLM)
English documentation not accessible; relying on Chinese official page
sources.notes: Product documentation in Chinese; describes feature set without effectiveness claims

sources.title: Using Study Mode in ChatGPT
directly_supported_observations: User can instruct system to guide thinking (Socratic), explain in layers, check understanding, or use hints/quizzes/step-by-step
User specifies level: middle school, high school, college, beginner, or advanced
User can request: slow down, simpler language, analogy, deeper explanation, more advanced content
Documentation states 'there may be times when it gives a direct answer' - Socratic not always applied
Can upload files (notes, syllabus, worksheet, slides, textbook excerpt, problem photos) and reference specific sections
Memory feature saves learning goals, preferred explanation style, or topics studied before
Documentation explicitly states Study Mode 'does not replace your teacher, tutor, course materials' and 'can make mistakes'
design_implications: User-requested controls documented (Socratic, layered explanation, hints) - design inference: whether explicit instruction is technically required vs. available option not directly stated
Documentation mentions possible direct answers alongside Socratic guidance - design inference: whether Socratic is opt-in/default-off vs. context-dependent not technically specified
User can request adjustments ('slow down', 'simpler') - design inference: whether automatic adjustment never occurs vs. not documented
Material grounding via file upload + manual section reference
Evidence collection sparse: observes completion and responses, does not infer mastery
limitations_and_non_inferences: No learning effectiveness claims provided
System does NOT automatically detect when to explain vs. hint vs. quiz
No learner modeling or knowledge state tracking described
Material constraint shallow: requires manual section pointing
Academic integrity boundaries unclear: 'Follow the AI-use policies of your school' - defers to external policy
sources.notes: Product documentation accessed 2026-07-29; document updated '23小时前' (23 hours ago) from access date

sources.title: Gemini 中的 LearnLM (LearnLM in Gemini)
directly_supported_observations: LearnLM built with education experts, optimized for learning based on rigorous research
Expert raters evaluated LearnLM against GPT-4o, Claude 3.5, Gemini 1.5 Pro on pedagogical elements like guidance and correcting mistakes beyond mere accuracy
RCT in Sierra Leone: 1,763 middle school students (grades 7-8), 8 weeks, 12+ hours usage minimum
Effect: math performance from 50th to 64th percentile (a difference of 14 percentile ranks)
Effect equivalent to 1.8 to 2.5 additional years of learning progress
With appropriate system instructions, Gemini leverages LearnLM learning science research to trigger pedagogical behaviors
Multiple technical reports cited: May 2026, November 2025, December 2024, May 2024
design_implications: Learning effectiveness measurable via RCT methodology in specific context
Pedagogical quality evaluated as separate dimension from accuracy
Learning science principles can be embedded in LLMs via training
System instructions enable pedagogical behavior activation
Minimum engagement threshold exists: 12+ hours over 8 weeks for observed effect
limitations_and_non_inferences: RCT context specific: Sierra Leone middle school students, math subject, 8-week period
Generalization to other contexts (subjects, age groups, countries) requires caution
Implementation details not disclosed in product page
Comparison baseline not specified ('from 50th to 64th percentile' - compared to what control group?)
Technical reports referenced but not directly linked in product page
sources.notes: Chinese official Google Cloud page; RCT conducted with Fab AI partnership; percentile positions not percentage points

sources.title: Tutor CoPilot: A Human-AI Approach for Scaling Real-Time Expertise
sources.organization_or_authors: Rose E. Wang, Ana T. Ribeiro, Carly D. Robinson, Susanna Loeb, Dorottya Demszky
directly_supported_observations: RCT with 700+ tutors and 1,000+ students from underserved communities
Students with tutors using Tutor CoPilot 4 percentage points more likely to master math topics (p<0.01)
Gains highest for students of lower-rated tutors: 9 percentage points
Analysis of 350,000+ messages shows system increases probing questions and reduces generic praise
System cost: approximately $20/tutor/year
System models expert thinking to assist tutors in real time
Human-AI collaboration: AI assists tutors who then interact with students (not direct AI-student)
design_implications: Human-AI collaboration model validated via RCT in real-world educational setting
AI assistance to human tutors produces measurable learning gains
System bridges skill gaps: larger gains for lower-rated tutors (9 p.p.) vs. average (4 p.p.)
Specific pedagogical behaviors measurable at message level: probing questions increase, generic praise decreases
Economic viability consideration: $20/tutor/year cited explicitly
limitations_and_non_inferences: Domain-specific: math tutoring in underserved communities
Tutor-mediated interaction, not direct AI-student tutoring
Implementation details not disclosed: how 'expert thinking' is modeled and delivered
Rating mechanism for tutors not specified
Mastery definition not provided in Stanford page abstract
sources.notes: Stanford SCALE Initiative publication, November 2025; download available at scale.stanford.edu/sites/default/files/ai24_1054_v2.pdf

sources.title: ALEKS Knowledge Space Theory
sources.organization_or_authors: McGraw Hill ALEKS / Jean-Paul Doignon, Jean-Claude Falmagne
directly_supported_observations: Knowledge Space Theory applies combinatorics and stochastic processes to modeling specific knowledge domains
Algebra 1 example: approximately 350 basic concepts giving rise to millions of empirically feasible knowledge states
Adaptive assessment using Markovian procedures can gauge student knowledge state in 25-30 questions despite millions of possible states
System determines 'precisely what each individual student knows, and what the student is ready to learn next'
Authoritative source: Learning Spaces by Doignon & Falmagne (Springer-Verlag, 2011)
Each domain (e.g., Algebra 1, Algebra 2) requires separate pre-built knowledge structure
design_implications: Knowledge modeling feasible at scale: 350 concepts → millions of states, assessment remains tractable (25-30 questions)
Prerequisite relationships mathematically modelable via combinatorial framework
Adaptive assessment can be efficient using stochastic (Markovian) procedures
Domain specificity critical: each course requires separate knowledge structure
'Ready to learn' is computable from knowledge state and structure
limitations_and_non_inferences: Learning effectiveness not claimed: describes assessment framework, not learning outcomes
Pedagogical action selection not addressed
Knowledge state construction method not detailed in product page
'Empirically feasible' knowledge state definition not provided
Question selection algorithm not disclosed
Granularity tradeoff unclear: is 350 concepts for Algebra 1 the right level?
sources.notes: Official ALEKS product page; theoretical foundation in Knowledge Space Theory (Doignon & Falmagne); product actively used in K-12 and higher education

sources.title: A Survey of Knowledge Tracing: Models, Variants, and Applications
sources.organization_or_authors: Shuanghong Shen, Qi Liu, Zhenya Huang, et al. / University of Science and Technology of China
directly_supported_observations: KT monitors evolving knowledge states during problem-solving; learning sequence formulated as interactions with exercises, KCs, correctness, and side information
Three model categories: Bayesian (BKT, DBKT), Logistic (LFA, PFA, KTM), Deep Learning (DKT, transformers)
Side information recorded: response time, opportunity count, tutor intervention, engagement metrics provide comprehensive reflection of learning process
Individualization variants: different students exhibit different learning rates and prior knowledge (DKT-DSC clustering, FGKT individual representations)
Exercise-level modeling: difficulty and discrimination parameters enhance performance; FGKT obtains individual exercise representation through knowledge cells
Forgetting variants: DKT-Forget integrates exponential decay; temporal gap between interactions affects retention
Applications (Section V): knowledge states enable adaptive resource recommendation and personalized learning path generation
design_implications: Interaction evidence: side information (response time, hints, attempts) provides richer signals than correctness alone
Learner state modeling at scale: deep learning tracks millions of knowledge states with tractable adaptive assessment
Task-specific modeling: exercise difficulty, discrimination, type explicitly modeled in variants
Temporal dynamics: forgetting curves, time gaps, opportunity counts affect knowledge state evolution
Domain-specific training: KT models require course-specific data (ASSISTments, EdNet datasets)
Evidence-based action: knowledge state estimates used for recommendation (application layer Section V)
limitations_and_non_inferences: Learning effectiveness: survey describes predictive accuracy, not direct learning outcome improvements from KT-guided interventions
Pedagogical action specification: models predict states; how to act is application layer
Cross-domain generalization: most datasets domain-specific (math tutoring); transfer not demonstrated
Real-time constraints: transformer computational complexity may prevent instant feedback
Cold-start problem: new students with no history require different approaches
Explainability tradeoff: deep models more accurate but less interpretable than Bayesian/logistic
sources.notes: arXiv v4 April 2024; IEEE Trans. journal version noted; full PDF downloaded via curl (7.5MB), pdftotext extraction (3,113 lines); verified problem definition, fundamental models, variants sections IV.A-D

sources.title: Open learner models and pedagogical strategies in higher education: a meta-synthesis
directly_supported_observations: Systematic review of 26 empirical studies on OLMs with pedagogical strategies in higher education (PROSPERO CRD420251237223)
Four OLM categories: Inspectable (view-only dashboards), Negotiable (bidirectional confidence calibration), Editable (learner modifies profile), Persuasive/Adaptive (AI/ML personalization)
Inspectable OLMs: transparency via dashboards; support performance/appraisal SRL phases; consistent gains in engagement, persistence, outcomes
Negotiable OLMs: dialogic feedback, confidence rating; improve confidence, self-assessment accuracy, motivation
Editable OLMs: goal-setting interfaces, portfolio systems; stronger initiative, ownership, persistence
Persuasive/Adaptive OLMs: intelligent tutoring systems, cognitive mapping, recommender algorithms; improvements in learning efficiency, time-on-task, cognitive engagement
Pedagogical strategies embedded: goal setting, reflective monitoring, confidence calibration, adaptive feedback, dialogic negotiation, performance visualization
design_implications: OLMs as metacognitive mediators (not purely analytical) when combined with pedagogical scaffolding
Learner agency continuum: system-guided reflection (inspectable) to learner-driven (editable) to adaptive co-regulation (AI-mediated)
Source-grounding + learner-model integration: inspectable OLMs visualize data; adaptive OLMs integrate learner models with content personalization
Evidence-based action: OLM feedback enables informed decisions; adaptive models automate action selection based on learner state
Transparency as pedagogy: making models transparent encourages metacognitive engagement and autonomy
Scaffolding requirement: editable OLMs need mediation to ensure reflective (not arbitrary) inputs
limitations_and_non_inferences: Domain specificity: STEM predominance may limit transferability to humanities/social sciences
Short-term interventions: most studies short-term; longitudinal SRL development unclear
SRL operationalization heterogeneity: varied measures constrain quantitative comparison
Affective dimensions underexplored: more cognitive/metacognitive focus than emotional regulation
Ethical AI concerns: algorithmic bias, data privacy, learner agency in persuasive models need research
Learning effectiveness vs. SRL support: SRL improvements demonstrated; direct outcome gains varied
sources.notes: Frontiers in Education Vol 10, published 2026-01-26 (DOI year 2025); full article (81KB) via rendered web fetch; meta-synthesis of 26 studies; four OLM categories, pedagogical strategies, SRL dimensions verified

sources.title: Predicting student outcomes using digital logs of learning behaviors: Review, current standards, and suggestions for future work
sources.organization_or_authors: Arizmendi CJ, Bernacki ML, Raković M, Plumley RD, Urban CJ, Panter AT, Greene JA, Gates KM
directly_supported_observations: LMS systems capture fine-grained learning activities with timestamps: frequency, time, patterns of interactions
Literature review: 39 papers, 82 predictive models; average accuracy 0.72 (SD=0.10) after 5.85 weeks (SD=3.67)
Three predictor categories: demographic, performance (prior grades/scores), behavioral trace data (LMS logs)
29 of 82 models used only behavioral predictors without demographics or grades
Behavioral trace data orthogonal to summative performance: views, downloads, submissions, forum contributions
Raw log data requires feature engineering: timestamps and actions mapped to meaningful measures using metadata
Metadata enrichment critical: semester alignment, file type, due date, relevance transforms raw events into predictive features
Machine learning for feature selection: embedded methods (decision trees, LASSO, elastic net) perform simultaneous selection and estimation
Model interpretability trade-off: regression coefficients explainable vs. neural networks high accuracy but black-box
Equity considerations: demographic variables raise concerns; recommendation is to test fairness across groups, not use demographics as features
Privacy expectations differ in education: students may not expect data collection similar to commercial web tracking
design_implications: Interaction evidence as learner state signal: LMS logs provide rich behavioral data beyond correctness
Feature engineering requirement: metadata-enriched mapping necessary to transform events into pedagogically interpretable measures
Temporal dynamics: early prediction (average 5.85 weeks) enables intervention before course completion
Model selection trade-offs: interpretable (elastic net) vs. high-accuracy black-box (neural nets); pedagogical applications may require explainability
Equity as design constraint: models must work equally well across demographic groups
Privacy-preserving design: educational data collection carries different expectations than commercial contexts
limitations_and_non_inferences: Review scope: single-course prediction in higher education; K-12, multi-course, longitudinal modeling unclear
Implementation details sparse: most papers report accuracy but not real-time vs. batch, computational costs, LMS integration
Causality not established: predictive models identify correlations; cannot infer behavior changes cause outcome improvements
Intervention effectiveness unknown: paper reviews prediction models, not intervention studies
Learning theory integration weak: many models data-driven with limited grounding in learning science
Context specificity: course type, student population, institution affect performance; cross-context generalization requires validation
Cold start problem: students with no interaction history cannot be modeled early
Temporal stability unknown: models may not generalize to future semesters as course design or population changes
sources.notes: Behavior Research Methods 2022-08-26; PMC10556130; 8 authors (Arizmendi, Bernacki, Raković, Plumley, Urban, Panter, Greene, Gates); full article 101 paragraphs ~80,500 chars via Europe PMC XML endpoint; direct URL blocked by CAPTCHA, XML fallback successful per Review 07 protocol; literature review of 39 papers, 82 models
